conventions.affiliations: Direct-kind sources follow the citations31 direct10 convention: an affiliation object is added only for an explicit, unambiguous attachment in the citation ("... of INSTITUTION" shared by the connected list, or a parenthetical after one name). creator426-kind sources follow their reviewed cohort notes, which add no affiliation objects; institutions stay in the preserved citation.
conventions.entity_category: A credit is admitted as organisational only when the record itself shows the named body acting (a laboratory, office, university, commission, agency named as the credited party). A credit that names a data collection, data product, satellite platform, forecast system or observation network is held: Zenodo creators are personal or organisational and the source does not supply that category.
conventions.honorific_rank_role: Honorifics (Dr., Mr.), military ranks (CWO3) and stated roles (editor) are not name parts. They are left out of the name fields and preserved verbatim in the preservation paragraph, as the citations31 policy did for FGDC-2597 ("Dr. Hatakeyama, former Director-General ..." -> Hatakeyama).
conventions.literal_conflict: A personal name whose literal spelling conflicts with the record's own embedded reference, the referenced work's byline or the record's own contact name is held (Navis/Davis, Uran/Urano, Bugae/Bugaev, Kandzela/Kondzela, Herman/Hermann). The project does not correct source text, and publishing a known-conflicting personal name needs an owner decision.
conventions.literal_parts: Creator names keep every literal source part in source order. No spelling is corrected, no initial is expanded, no person is added from a contact, abstract or external work, and no entity type is inferred from a name alone.
conventions.name_parts: A person is split into family and given names only when the record settles the boundary: an inverted form in the citation or embedded reference, an initials-plus-family pattern, a matching inverted contact name, or an honorific that fixes natural order (Mr./Dr. Given Family).
conventions.particle: A nobility particle stays where the source's own inverted form puts it ("Boguslawski, G. Von" -> family_name "Boguslawski", given_name "G. Von").
conventions.preservation_paragraph: Every admitted source carries one paragraph, rendered into the v1 preservation block as the citations31 policy does, that quotes the complete literal credit and states what was left out of the name fields.
conventions.scope: Only the exact 64 sources: remaining100 of the program20 reconciliation minus the 31 citations31 members minus the five protected records. Every one is a supported singleton in the frozen publication plan; none is in the remaining45 (39 held, 6 failed).
conventions.suffix: Generational suffixes (Jr., III) stay with the given names in the inverted citation form the sources themselves use ("Farley, E.V., Jr."): family_name "Farley", given_name "Edward V., Jr.". The provider displays family_name, given_name, so the record reads "Farley, Edward V., Jr." and the DataCite familyName stays the family name. This is a representation convention for the independent reviewer to confirm, not a claim that the suffix is a given name; InvenioRDM has no suffix field.
